attributes.board_name: South Carolina Board of Medical Examiners (SC LLR)

rules.accepted_credit_types: Category I CME sponsored by the AMA, AOA or another organization approved by the board; at least 30 hours directly related to the licensee's practice area
rules.alternatives: Instead of 40 hours, one of: certification of added qualifications or recertification after examination by an ABMS/AOA or other approved specialty board; completion of an ACGME/AOA-approved US or Canadian residency or fellowship; passing SPEX or COMVEX; or a board-approved clinical skills assessment program (e.g. CPEP).
rules.new_licensee_rule: For a license first issued during a biennial renewal period, meeting the initial licensure requirements is sufficient for the first renewal.
rules.audit_note: Completion certified under oath on the renewal application; random Board audits. Statute requires the controlled-substance certificate with each renewal.

topics.who: All MD/DO: prescribing and monitoring Schedule II-IV controlled substances, part of the 40 h; non-prescribers may use accredited education on controlled substances, abuse, diversion and treatment

Emergency medicine, primary care, internal/family medicine, pediatrics, OB/GYN, hospitalists, and those in public health clinics, EDs, urgent care and community-based centers. Due before Jan 1, 2028 (licensed before Jan 1, 2026) or within 2 years of initial licensure, then every 6 years

rules.notes: One board licenses MD and DO; renewal every 2 years by June 30 of odd-numbered years. 30 of 40 h in specialty; up to 10 h for volunteer medical service (§ 38-79-30). Non-prescribers may meet the 2 h with general controlled-substance education (Board statement 2023).
rules.rule_quote: (2) For renewal of an active permanent license biennially, documented evidence of at least one of following options during the renewal period is required: (a) forty hours of Category I continuing medical education…
